title: Module Version Garden: Versioning & Publish Flows (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This note captures an experimental, pragmatic approach we can trial for Terraform module versioning, registry publishing, and controlled breaking-change rollout for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. It mixes semver + compatibility gates + migration helpers so module consumers can upgrade with low blast radius.

Scope:
- All internal terraform modules that are consumed by Private deployment packaging or customer onprem bundles.
- Excludes ephemeral demo scripts and one-off prototypes.

High level idea - the "Version Garden":
- Keep a simple mainline (vN.x) garden bed per module: stable branch (vX) + experimental sidebeds (alpha/beta).
- Encourage small incremental bumps and clear migration paths; breaking changes require a formal gate and migration helper.

Versioning policy (practical semver):
- MAJOR (X+): breaking API changes to module inputs/outputs or state layout. Only used after completing the Breaking-Change Checklist below.
- MINOR (x.Y): additive features, optional inputs with safe defaults. Should be backwards compatible.
- PATCH (x.y.Z): bug fixes, docs, internal refactors that do not change API or state.
- Pre-release tags: alpha/beta (e.g., 2.3.0-beta.1) for experimental features behind a feature flag.

Compatibility gates (automated checks):
- Static contract tests: syntactic validation of inputs/outputs against a contract file (module.contract.json stored in repo root).
- State-migration smoke tests: small e2e that runs plan/apply against a disposable state snapshot to detect resource rename/delete risks.
- Downstream consumer matrix: for each public module we run a matrix of 3 consumer archetypes (simple, multi-region, onprem-enterprise) in CI.

Registry publish pipeline (high-level):
1) Branch + PR with changelog entry and migration notes. PR must include CONTRACT diff (if changing inputs/outputs).
2) CI runs: fmt/lint/tflint/contract-checks/static-tests + consumer matrix.
3) If tests pass and change is non-breaking -> tag release and publish to internal registry (registry.redwood.local).
4) Breaking changes: block automatic publish. Author must open an upgrade plan ticket, attach migration scripts and schedule a staged rollout.

Breaking-Change Checklist (required before MAJOR bump):
- [ ] Document the exact user-visible change (inputs/outputs/state) in the PR description.
- [ ] Provide automated migration script (terraform state mv or import helpers) and test it in CI.
- [ ] Add a compatibility shim where possible (legacy input alias) for one minor release cycle.
- [ ] Run consumer matrix with the new version and with old consumer code to validate failure modes.
- [ ] Create Upgrade Playbook (short doc): impact, rollback steps, alerting, contact list.
- [ ] Communicate change on #infra-modules Slack, include affected module users, and create a JIRA INFRA ticket with rollout schedule.
- [ ] Run a staged rollout: canary customers -> internal teams -> broader customers. Record telemetry.

Migration helper patterns (examples):
- Input alias shim: if "instance_count" is renamed to "replica_count", accept both for one release:
  variable "instance_count" { type = number, default = null }
  variable "replica_count" { type = number, default = null }
  locals { replicas = var.replica_count != null ? var.replica_count : var.instance_count }
- State rename helper (recommended): provide a script (bash + terraform state mv) that maps old resource addresses to new ones and run in CI.

Consumer pinning guidance:
- Consumers should pin module versions explicitly in prod (e.g., source = "registry.redwood.local/redwood/vpc/aws" version = "~> 2.1") and test minor bumps in staging first.
- Provide a simple upgrade checklist in the module README with sample terraform constraint patterns.

Changelog template (to include in PR):
- Summary (one sentence)
- Type: patch|minor|major|docs
- Migration steps (if any)
- Impacted resources/list of adopters (best-effort)
- Rollout plan (canary list + dates)

Example registry publish CLI snippet (internal):
- Build artifact: make release-artifact
- Run contract checks: ./scripts/contract-verify.sh
- Publish: registryctl publish --module ./ --version 2.3.0 --registry https://registry.redwood.local

Rollback and emergency flow:
- If rollout fails, revert to previous published module version and open hotfix branch.
- For state-corrupting changes we must provide an emergency remediation script and contact SRE oncall.

Communication and cadence:
- Weekly module owners sync (15 min) to surface upcoming breaking changes.
- Monthly registry audit: unused modules, stale pre-releases.

Open questions / things to iterate:
- Do we want an explicit "compatibility file" format (JSON Schema or HCL) to define allowed input types and defaults? (pro: machine-checkable; con: extra maintenance)
- How long do we maintain shims/aliases? Recommended: 1 minor cycle (approx 8 weeks).
- Do we automate consumer-notification based on CODEOWNERS in downstream repos?

Next immediate actions (for this WIP):
- Add contract-checker prototype to infra-modules CI (owner: Arjun)
- Create a repo template for migration-scripts with examples (owner: Maya)
- Draft a short Upgrade Playbook template for module PRs (owner: Sofia)

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep module READMEs explicit about stateful changes.
- Prefer additive changes and feature flags in private deployments to reduce onprem risk.
- Try the policy on 2 low-risk modules first (networking, monitoring).

References & example artifacts:
- GH PR with a sample shim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/482
- Example migration script (draft): scripts/migrate-rename-resource.sh
- Staging consumer matrix job: .github/workflows/consumer-matrix.yml

-- end --
